title: Late Breaking Results: Decentralized Voting-Based Attestation for IoT Devices
problem: Traditional remote attestation (RA) schemes for IoT rely on a single trusted verifier, creating a single point of failure and security vulnerability.
motivation: IoT device security is often neglected during manufacturing; a decentralized attestation mechanism would eliminate single points of failure.
method: Proposes voting-based blockchain attestation protocol where distributed verification occurs across all nodes, creating immutable traceable attestation history accessible to auditors.
key_novelty: Decentralized voting-based blockchain protocol eliminates single-point-of-failure in remote attestation for IoT.
contributions: Distributed verification across all nodes eliminates single point of failure
Traceable and immutable public attestation history
Enables external auditor verification at any time
Prototype implementation on three NVIDIA Jetson embedded devices with up to 15 attestation nodes

metrics.other: verified on NVIDIA Jetson embedded devices

limitations: Late-breaking work; limited to 15 nodes on Jetson devices; scalability and performance overhead not discussed.
